Real adapter over the fake MCP server, no injected fault, lease 45s, set = {issue description, marker A} (one target, so one marker per grant), two overlapping acquisitions by ONE holder: `await asyncio.gather(a.acquire_surfaces(surfaces=want, holder='job-a', lease_seconds=45), b.acquire_surfaces(surfaces=want, holder='job-a', lease_seconds=45))`. Observed deterministically (5/5 repeats): both calls RETURN a `SurfaceLease` for job-a (`expires_at` 12:00:45); ZERO markers stand afterwards; job-b's `acquire_surfaces` over the SAME set is then GRANTED — no `SurfaceLeaseError`, no refusal, no naming. So job-a holds two leases over a set job-b also holds, and the intersection is not discovered at acquisition — the sentence the Do clause turns on ("contention is discovered at acquisition, never at write time"), and with it "Acquisition is all-or-nothing ... and afterwards holds nothing".; repaired 41f2f8a + 14268d9 (head 1e69845) — reproduced first at e1953f5 with my own numbers (lease 90s, holder `runner-one`, set = {issue description, marker `plan`}, two `LinearMcpTracker` instances over one fake MCP server with both creations held at a barrier until both were on the board): both `acquire_surfaces` calls returned a `SurfaceLease`, ZERO markers stood, a DIFFERENT holder then took the whole set with no refusal and no naming, and the original holder's `renew_surfaces` → None. Deterministic 5/5. The same construction on claims annihilated the claim too.

The defect was not in the acquisition path but in the tie-break being applied to a holder's own second grant: each retracted the other's marker. A holder identity is exactly what the arbitration is over, so a second grant to it is the same ownership observed twice rather than contention to discover. `domain/surface_lease.one_ownership` states it once — the grant the backend ordered FIRST stands for both, every later one withdraws INTO it — and the adapter applies it over the WHOLE grant rather than per target, so a set spanning two logs cannot be split between one holder's own two grants and halved. Contention between DIFFERENT holders is untouched: an intersecting set is still refused at acquisition naming the owner, a set two holders reach at one instant is still a tie both withdraw from, and each is earliest on a different target both still withdraw.

Measured on the real board and pinned rather than assumed (14268d9): when the log hid each grant's confirmation from the other's read-back, both stood and two markers of ONE holder were left. That is a duplicate and not a second owner — no other holder can take any part of the set, every reader names the same holder, and the marker nothing renews lapses.
